topic: Moli: The Best Browser for AI Agents, Written in Pure Rust

key_points: Chrome is a 300MB binary built to render cat videos and run Google Docs — a sledgehammer for AI scraping workloads
Obscura: Rust + V8, 30MB memory vs Chrome 200+, 70MB binary, 85ms page load, native anti-detection via --stealth flag, CDP-compatible with Puppeteer/Playwright
Lightpanda: written in Zig from scratch (not a Chromium fork), uses html5ever + V8 + libcurl, 11x faster than headless Chrome and 9x less memory on 100-page Puppeteer tests
Steel Browser: wraps headless Chrome in an agent-purpose-built API layer (Chrome-as-a-Service)
50,000+ developers use headless browsers for AI agents; 150k+ total stars across the 4 main tools
Lightpanda: 17k+ stars, Go-based, 9x less memory, 11x faster startup, native MCP server + CDP support, built specifically for AI agents
Playwright: 14k+ stars, general-purpose modern web testing; Puppeteer 110k+ stars; Selenium 30k+ multi-language
Key differentiator for AI: memory footprint and cold-start speed determine how many concurrent agent instances you can run
AI browser market projected to grow from $4.5B in 2024 to $76.8B by 2034 (32.8% CAGR); 79% of companies have adopted some form of AI agent technology
Browser Use hit 97,000+ stars and Firecrawl crossed 130,000+, both in GitHub's top 100 repos
Browser agents fall into three buckets: AI-assisted consumer browsers (Comet, Atlas, Dia, Opera Neon), open-source agent frameworks (Browser Use), and infrastructure platforms
Real-world use: agents navigate, click, extract, run code, test flows, and record video walkthroughs end-to-end

Decision tree: AI agent controlling browser → agent-browser (accessibility-tree-based navigation); bulk crawling/scraping → Lightpanda (ultra-lightweight headless engine); E2E testing → Playwright (de-facto standard)
Tools operate at different layers of the stack — positioning matters more than raw features
Same task (extracting top 5 HN posts) implemented in Playwright (TypeScript), agent-browser (CLI), and Lightpanda (direct CDP calls) to compare approaches
Moli is a web-extraction-first headless browser built in Rust — runs real JavaScript, implements Web APIs and CSS behavior extraction workflows observe
Deliberately avoids the full layout, compositor, GPU, media, and rendering stack that most web data pipelines throw away
Two operating modes: 'moli fetch' (one-shot URL→HTML/text extraction) and 'moli serve' (long-running CDP automation service on port 9222)
Stealth-conscious defaults: browser-like client defaults, high-quality user agent surface, stable automation behavior

stats.fact: On the Web Crawling mixed public-URL benchmark (n=192), Moli produced 103 useful pages (53.6% success) at 73 MiB median RSS, vs Chrome's 101 pages (52.6%) at 773 MiB — roughly one-tenth the memory footprint
Moli median page time was 1.43s, matching Chrome's 1.43s, while Lightpanda was faster at 0.97s but only produced 85 useful pages (44.3%) and Obscura 57 pages (29.7%)
Moli v0.1.0 released 2026-05-25 with prebuilt binaries for Linux x64 (96MB), Apple x64 (88MB), and Apple aarch64 (84MB)
Lightpanda (lightpanda-io/browser) has 33,795 GitHub stars and is written in Zig; Obscura (h4ckf0r0day/obscura) has 21,207 stars and is written in Rust
Playwright (microsoft/playwright) has 94,337 stars; Browser Use (browser-use/browser-use) has 108,740 stars
The AI browser market is projected to grow from $4.5B in 2024 to $76.8B by 2034 (32.8% CAGR), and 79% of companies have adopted some form of AI agent technology

angles: Moli is the only Rust headless browser that keeps Chrome-level extraction yield (103 useful pages) while cutting memory to ~1/10th (73 MiB vs 773 MiB) — the 'best of both worlds' vs Lightpanda/Obscura which trade yield for memory
Positioning: Moli is web-extraction-first, not a screenshot browser — it skips the expensive visual rendering stack data pipelines discard, which is the core architectural bet
Stealth-conscious defaults make Moli practical for real sites that gate content behind browser-like behavior, unlike raw HTTP fetchers with JS bolted on
CDP 'serve' mode means existing Puppeteer/Playwright automation can attach to Moli with minimal changes — a low-friction migration story
Rust runtime = predictable performance, memory safety, and production-grade concurrency for large queues and long-lived workers
The benchmark story is the hook: Moli beats Chrome on yield AND memory, and beats Lightpanda/Obscura on yield while staying lean
